lines.text: Fieldday is five people running a 15,000-a-day festival. For ten weeks they say yes: in emails, on calls, in contracts. Nobody writes those promises down in one place.
We gave it 25 real-looking conversations. It found 39 promises. Six of them can't all be kept.
Five different people each handed out a few parking passes. Every one was reasonable. Together it's 41 passes for a 30-space lot.
Every promise links back to the exact sentence it came from, so you never have to trust the AI's word for it.
Priya gave Marlo Vance the green room from 5:30. Sam gave Halfmoon Parade the same room from 6. Neither knew.
The contract says 60 minutes. A friendly email a week later says 75. The artist will hold us to the email.
And this one: "we'll sort a vegan caterer." Promised by the director, owned by nobody.
Now a new email comes in. Mei promises a buggy for Saturday. All four buggies were already promised.
The ledger catches it the moment it's said, not on show day.
It drafts the awkward email for you. It never sends anything.
How it works: the AI only reads and extracts. Plain code does the counting and decides what clashes, so a hallucination can't invent a problem or hide one.
The Promise Ledger. Know what you've said yes to.
